title: Each dot is one thing, measured two ways

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A scatter plot shows whether two measurements go together.

do.text: Do the two measurements go together?
do.label: The question

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten students: the hours each one studied,

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: and the score each one got on a test.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The first studied two hours: across to two,

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: then up to the score, fifty-seven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The second: five hours, seventy-six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The third: seven hours, eighty-five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Then the other seven, one after another.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten dots: each dot is one student.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Together, the dots make a cloud, and this cloud climbs.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Measurements that go together have an association. More hours tended to come with higher scores: a positive association.

do.meaning: As one measurement goes up, the other tends to go up.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Tended to, not always: this student studied eight hours,

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: but scored lower than one who studied five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: An association is a pattern in the whole cloud, not a promise about every dot.

do.text: A pattern in the whole cloud,
not a promise about every dot

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The dots stay near a straight band: a linear association.

do.meaning: The dots stay near a straight band.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now a lemonade stand: the price of a cup, and the cups sold, on sixteen days.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This cloud falls from left to right.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Higher prices tended to come with fewer cups sold: a negative association.

do.meaning: As one measurement goes up, the other tends to go down.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A common slip calls this no association, because the dots are not on one line.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: But an association never needs one line. The whole cloud falls, so it is negative.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Fourteen students: the day of the month each was born, and a quiz score.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This cloud has no tilt: high and low scores turn up all through the month.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Knowing a birthday tells nothing about a score: no association.

do.meaning: Knowing one measurement tells nothing about the other.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A puppy, weighed each month for a year.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: It gains fast, then slower, so the dots follow a curve: a nonlinear association.

do.meaning: The dots follow a curve, not a straight band.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Thirteen students: miles from school, and minutes to get there.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One dot sits far from the rest. A dot like that is an outlier.

do.meaning: A dot far from the rest of the cloud.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The weights and heights of eleven dogs.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Small dogs bunch here, and big dogs there. A bunch apart from the others is a cluster.

do.meaning: A bunch of dots apart from the others.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Climbing is positive, falling is negative, and no tilt is none.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A straight band is linear; a bend is nonlinear.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each dot is one thing, measured two ways. The tilt of the cloud is the association.
